title: How to Stop Worrying and Start Living
author: Dale Carnegie
blurb: Dale Carnegie wrote this book after seeing how much worry quietly ruined people's lives, including his own students'. He gathered stories from ordinary people and famous figures, plus wisdom from philosophers and doctors, and boiled it down to simple habits anyone can use. He says to live one day at a time instead of drowning in past regrets and future fears. He gives a step-by-step method for facing problems: get the facts, decide, then act. He urges readers to stay busy, check the odds before panicking, accept what cannot be changed, and stop replaying old mistakes. He also argues that our thoughts shape our happiness, so we should count our blessings and turn setbacks into gains. Finally, he shows that helping others is one of the surest cures for worry.

lessons.b: Close the doors on yesterday and tomorrow and give your full attention to today, because that is the only day you can actually live.
Ask what the worst possible outcome is, accept it in your mind, then calmly work to improve on it.

lessons.b: Most worry comes from confusion, so write down the facts, decide what to do, and act on that decision right away.

lessons.t: Let the Law of Averages Calm You
lessons.b: When you check the real odds, most of the things you dread turn out to be very unlikely to happen.
Accept what you cannot change, set a limit on how much worry anything deserves, and stop replaying mistakes you cannot undo.
issues: scene 1: The 'ATTIC' label inside the house roof is very small, about 14px at 1600 width, which is below the 18px minimum. (fix: Increase the 'ATTIC' label to at least 18–20px. Move it beside the attic window if it no longer fits inside the gable.)

lessons.b: Your thoughts shape your mood, so focus on what is going right and look for ways to turn losses into gains.
Doing something kind for someone else each day pulls you out of your own worries and ties all of Carnegie's habits into a happier life.
